question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)+{y}^{2}(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)-{y}^{2}(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Given the system of differential equations, select the correct options below.

The Jacobian determinant of the system at the equilibrium point ${x}^{∗}=[0,\text{ }0]^{T}$ is given as

$$
J(0,0)={{field-1}}.
$$

At this point, the system is 
{{field-2}}
at ${x}^{∗}.$
question.worked_solution:
The system can be rewritten in matrix form as 

$$
{x}^{′}=\text{\boldsymbol}f(x)
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and 
$\text{\boldsymbol}f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\end{aligned}].$

We need to compute the Jacobian determinant of $\text{\boldsymbol}f(x).$ 

In our case, we have the following:

$$
J=|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}|
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})=2x,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})=2y \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=2x,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2y\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we have

$$
J=|\begin{aligned}2x & 2y \\ 2x & -2y\end{aligned}|.
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}J(0,0) & =|\begin{aligned}2(0) & 2(0) \\ 2(0) & -2(0)\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the Jacobian determinant is zero, our system is $\text{not almost linear}$ at ${x}^{∗}.$
